newsitem.title: USA: Illinois Medicare providers notified in lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Illinois Medicare providers notified in lawsuit.

text.p: Medicare providers in Illinois are being notified by both the state and by filers of a class-action lawsuit that they could be eligible for higher reimbursements from the state.

The notification process followed an Aug. 2 ruling by a U.S. District Court judge in Chicago that found the Illinois Department of Public Aid had been shortchanging providers of Medicare services to the elderly poor.

Judge Robert Gettleman ordered the state to pay 100 percent of the reimbursements due the providers, which include more than 25,000 hospitals, clinics, physicians, medical supply companies and other health care companies.

However, that order was stayed pending an appeal. The state filed an appeal with the U.S. Court of Apeals for the Seventh Circuit on Sept. 30, according to Dean Schott, a spokesman for the public aid department.

Schott said ads were run by the department late last month in local newspapers informing Medicare providers about the federal court ruling and advising them to contact attorneys who filed the class-action lawsuit for more information.
Meanwhile, those attorneys at Levenfeld, Eisenberg, Janger & Glassberg issued a news release Tuesday that gave out a phone number and Internet address that Medicare providers can contact.
According to the news release, if Judge Gettleman's ruling is upheld on appeal, Medicare providers in Illinois could receive an additional $70 million more a year in reimbursements from the state.

Meanwhile, a lawsuit seeking retroactive Medicare payments from Illinois is pending in Cook County Circuit Court. That lawsuit could cover as much as seven years of payments, according to an attorney representing the providers.
Schott said the public aid department had not made any estimates on how much either lawsuit could cost the state prospectively or retroactively.
